Data Storage & External Services

The application has no relational database or local persistence layer. Azure Cognitive Search stores job postings and ZIP-code geospatial documents in separate indexes. The DataLoader utility seeds those indexes from schema and JSON files in the web project. The browser calls Bing Maps to visualize search results.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Search and geospatial lookup are implemented directly through Azure Cognitive Search; no repository or ORM layer is present.
  • Job search and the sample-data loader are separate projects and are deployed/run independently.
  • The web client composes search responses into HTML and map pins in the browser.

DTOs & Contracts

NYCJob is the web search response model, NYCJobLookup is the single-document lookup response model, and Azure SDK SearchDocument/SearchResult types carry indexed data. These mutable C# classes expose public setters. Search and suggestion inputs are ordinary MVC query/form parameters rather than dedicated request DTOs. No OpenAPI, protobuf, or GraphQL contract was found. The DataLoader uses Newtonsoft.Json serialization for its REST request helper.

Communication Patterns

The browser calls MVC actions synchronously over HTTP. The controller delegates to JobsSearch, which makes synchronous SDK calls to Azure Cognitive Search for jobs, ZIP-code geocoding, suggestions, and document lookup. The DataLoader uses synchronous HttpClient.SendAsync(...).Result REST calls over an explicitly constructed HTTPS service URI. No message broker, service discovery, API gateway, client-side load balancing, timeout policy, retry policy, circuit breaker, or configured fallback was found. No authentication or authorization is implemented for the MVC actions; Azure Search credentials are configured separately, while a map credential is embedded in client code. No TLS configuration for the web host is evidenced in the repository.

Core Business Workflows

JobSearch helps people discover New York City job postings by keyword, job attributes, and location, and lets them inspect an individual posting. A companion console utility refreshes the search indexes from bundled sample data.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
Job postingNYCJobsWeb / Job DiscoveryPublic listing describing an available city job and its posting detailsHas a geospatial location used for map display and distance filtering
ZIP-code documentNYCJobsWeb / Location SearchZIP code and geographic coordinates used to resolve a search originSupplies a coordinate to nearby job searches; stored in a separate search index
Search resultNYCJobsWeb / Job DiscoveryA job posting returned with facets and result countGroups postings with facets and pagination metadata

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
NYCJobsWebJob Discovery and Location SearchReads job postings and ZIP-code documents; no write ownershipAzure Cognitive Search, Bing Maps
DataLoaderSearch Index ProvisioningCreates and populates job and ZIP-code indexesAzure Cognitive Search and repository sample data

The search indexes are the source of truth for the demo's searchable records. DataLoader is a separate operational utility that replaces index content; no domain data is exchanged between the two projects except through the shared indexes and static files.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Search and filter job postings

  1. A visitor enters a keyword or accepts the default all-jobs search, then optionally selects facets, sorting, pagination, or a location radius.
  2. The browser posts criteria to the MVC search action.
  3. The application converts a blank keyword to a wildcard search. When distance is requested, it first looks up the ZIP-code document to obtain coordinates.
  4. The search layer queries the job index with selected facets/sort order and optional geospatial filtering.
  5. The response returns documents, available facets, and a result count; the browser displays listings, facets, pages, and map pins.

Workflow 2: Inspect or find a job title

The visitor opens a job detail view, which requests a document by identifier. As the visitor types, the suggestion action requests fuzzy or exact suggestions from the search service and returns suggestion text to the browser.

Workflow 3: Refresh sample search indexes

An operator runs DataLoader with target service settings. The utility deletes and recreates the ZIP-code and job indexes using local schema files, then uploads matching JSON files. Errors are printed to the console; the operation is destructive to existing index contents.

Cross-Service Data Flows

NYCJobsWeb first obtains ZIP-code coordinates from the zipcodes index when a radius search is enabled, then uses the location in a geospatial filter against the nycjobs index. Job results are returned as search documents and rendered in a browser map. DataLoader accesses the same indexes directly to replace and repopulate their contents. These are shared external search resources rather than inter-service HTTP calls; no circuit breaker or fallback response is implemented.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Visitor as "Job seeker" participant Browser as "Search page" participant Web as "NYCJobsWeb" participant Search as "Azure Cognitive Search" participant Map as "Bing Maps" Visitor->>Browser: Enter query and optional filters Browser->>Web: Submit search request alt Location radius selected Web->>Search: Find ZIP code coordinates Search-->>Web: ZIP code location Web->>Search: Search postings near location else No location radius Web->>Search: Search postings with text and facets end Search-->>Web: Postings, facets, and count Web-->>Browser: JSON search response Browser->>Browser: Render listings, facets, and pagination Browser->>Map: Show posting locations Visitor->>Browser: Select a posting Browser->>Web: Request posting by document id Web->>Search: Retrieve job document Search-->>Web: Job posting Web-->>Browser: JSON details response

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Blank search text becomes a wildcard, allowing the visitor to browse all indexed jobs.
  • Optional business-title, posting-type, salary, and geographic criteria are combined into a search filter.
  • The location workflow only looks up a ZIP code when maximum distance is positive; the resulting coordinates determine the proximity filter.
  • Results use ten records per page and may be sorted by featured score, salary, or posting date.
  • Suggestions can use fuzzy matching; duplicate suggestion strings are removed before responding.
  • No user accounts, eligibility checks, payment flows, authorization rules, transaction boundaries, audit trail, or explicit business-level input validation are present.

Version & Compatibility Risks

Both projects target .NET Framework rather than modern .NET. Several packages are old; the declared Newtonsoft.Json 9.0.1/10.0.3 versions and System.Text.Encodings.Web 4.6.0 are affected by advisories recorded in the accompanying security assessment. The web application also uses ASP.NET MVC 5, which requires a migration path rather than a direct ASP.NET Core package update.

Notable Observations

  • Newtonsoft.Json is independently declared at two versions across the two projects.
  • The browser stack includes jQuery 3.1.1 and Bootstrap 3.4.1.
  • The web application references both Azure SDK packages and older Microsoft REST client libraries.

The data layer consists of two Azure Cognitive Search indexes for job-posting documents and ZIP-code/geospatial documents; there is no relational database or ORM entity layer. The application queries those indexes directly, while the DataLoader imports schema definitions and sample JSON files.

Caching Strategy

No cache provider, cache annotations, in-memory cache, or distributed cache configuration was found. Search requests are sent to Azure Cognitive Search directly.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The web application and DataLoader access the same two Azure Search indexes but serve different roles: the web application reads documents, and the utility creates/replaces indexes and imports sample data. They share the schema and sample data files in the repository; no cross-service database joins or event-driven data exchange are present. Search results and ZIP-code coordinates are composed in the web search flow, with the ZIP-code lookup used to calculate a geographic filter for the job index.
